summary: Specifies the Minimum Rank with Hysteresis Objective Function (MRHOF) for RPL, the routing protocol for low-power and lossy networks. It selects routes that minimize a metric while using hysteresis to reduce churn in the chosen path. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: When picking the best path to school, you do not switch every time another path is only a tiny bit better. This rule makes devices stick to a good path unless the new one is clearly better.

questions: how does rpl avoid route flapping
subtitle: A route-selection rule for RPL that picks the cheapest path but only switches parents when the gain is big enough.

tldr.problem: RPL needs an Objective Function to decide which routes to use, and in low-power lossy networks small metric changes could make nodes flip between paths constantly.
tldr.mechanism: MRHOF picks the parent with the lowest path cost for an additive metric such as ETX, latency or hop count, and only switches away from the current parent if the new path is better by at least PARENT_SWITCH_THRESHOLD.
tldr.outcome: Networks get stable minimum-cost paths. It works only with additive metrics, defaults to ETX when no metric container is present, and has IANA Objective Code Point 1.

today: RFC 6719 is a Proposed Standard published in September 2012, and the data shows no RFC obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Objective Functions and the Role of MRHOF
sections.content:
An Objective Function tells RPL (RFC 6550) how to select paths. If it minimizes hop count, RPL picks minimum hop-count paths. Nodes may use metrics for links or nodes (RFC 6551), advertised in DIO messages inside a Metric Container. To keep routing independent of any one metric, RPL describes routes with a value called Rank, which roughly corresponds to distance. The Objective Function defines how a node computes its Rank. RPL requires all nodes in a network to use the same Objective Function.

The Minimum Rank with Hysteresis Objective Function (MRHOF) selects the path with the smallest metric value and uses hysteresis to avoid churn. Which metric it minimizes depends on what the DIO Metric Container advertises, for example latency or Expected Transmission Count (ETX). With no metric or container, MRHOF defaults to ETX. Because it minimizes path cost, it works only with additive metrics.
sections.eli5: Devices in a small wireless network each need to choose who to pass messages to. MRHOF is the rule they all follow to choose well and not keep changing their minds.

sections.title: Key Terms
sections.content:
The RFC introduces three terms. The selected metric is the single metric the operator chose for path selection; it is indicated by being present in the DIO Metric Container, while ETX is indicated by the absence of the container. Path cost is the sum of the selected link metric and the path cost advertised by the parent. The worst parent is the node in the parent set with the largest path cost.

In this document, Rank means the value of the Rank field, not DAGRank as in RFC 6550.
sections.eli5: Path cost is like the total travel time to the destination, adding up each leg of the trip.

sections.title: Path Cost and Parent Selection
sections.content:
A non-root node computes the path cost through each candidate neighbor by adding the selected metric for the link (or node) to the metric in the DIO sent by that neighbor. If the node has no metrics for any candidate, it MUST join a neighbor as a RPL Leaf. If the link metric is unavailable, the cost through that neighbor SHOULD be set to MAX_PATH_COST, which keeps the path out of consideration. Costs SHOULD be recomputed when a metric changes or a new advertisement arrives, and also periodically.

Parent selection SHOULD run when a candidate's path cost changes or a new candidate appears. A node MUST pick the candidate with the lowest path cost, with exceptions. The hysteresis exception is the key one: if the best path is cheaper than cur_min_path_cost by less than PARENT_SWITCH_THRESHOLD, the node MAY keep its current preferred parent. Links above MAX_LINK_METRIC SHOULD be excluded. A node MAY declare itself a Floating root in some cases.

A node MAY also keep up to PARENT_SET_SIZE minus 1 extra candidates in its parent set, each costing no more than any node outside the set.
sections.eli5: You only change your walking route if the new one saves you a good chunk of time, not just a few seconds.

sections.title: Computing and Advertising Rank
sections.content:
DAG roots set their Rank to MinHopRankIncrease. For other nodes, Table 1 converts a parent's path cost to Rank: hop count and ETX use the cost directly, and latency uses cost divided by 65536. For any other metric the Rank is undefined and the node must join as a Leaf.

A node sets its Rank to the maximum of three values: the Rank through the preferred parent, the highest advertised Rank in the parent set rounded up to the next multiple of MinHopRankIncrease, and the largest calculated Rank among paths through the parent set minus MaxRankIncrease. The third case keeps the node from advertising a Rank that rules out members of its parent set, but it can make the advertised Rank much higher than the real one, so a parent set with widely varying Ranks may cause suboptimal routing.

What a node advertises in its metric container is the path cost of the parent-set member with the highest cost. If ETX is the selected metric, the node MUST NOT put it in a container. It advertises an approximation as Rank, using Rank equal to ETX * 128, and MRHOF MUST ignore any ETX value in a received container.
sections.eli5: Each device tells its neighbors a cautious number for how far it is from the goal, so neighbors do not count on a shortcut that might not hold.

sections.title: Parameters and Recommended Values
sections.content:
MRHOF keeps one variable, cur_min_path_cost, the cost through the preferred parent at the last selection. It has five parameters, whose best values depend on the deployment and selected metric: MAX_LINK_METRIC, MAX_PATH_COST, PARENT_SWITCH_THRESHOLD, PARENT_SET_SIZE and ALLOW_FLOATING_ROOT.

When ETX is the selected metric, the RFC RECOMMENDS the values in the table, based on working group experience. Implementations SHOULD allow these parameters to be configured at installation time and MAY allow changes at run time. Unless configured otherwise they SHOULD use these defaults.
sections.eli5: These are the dials on the rule: how bad a road can be, how much better a new road must be, and how many backup roads to keep.

sections.title: Manageability and Metric Maximization
sections.content:
An implementation MUST support the DODAG Configuration option from RFC 6550. Care is needed in how PARENT_SWITCH_THRESHOLD relates to MaxRankIncrease: if the latter is smaller, a node could stay with a parent that pushes its Rank beyond the limit and drop out of the topology even though another parent-set member would keep it in. A large MinHopRankIncrease makes MRHOF unable to separate paths with different hop counts but similar metrics, so the advertised Rank becomes a simple hop count.

Metrics that must be maximized, such as path reliability, cannot be used directly. They can be converted to minimization if there is a fixed, well-known best value (the cost at the root) and all values are negative, for example the logarithm of link reliability, which is 0 at best. Implementations should also expose DAG information and a neighbor list for monitoring.
sections.eli5: Setting the dials wrongly can make a device stubbornly keep a bad road and get lost, so the dials need to fit together.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
MRHOF introduces no new flows or messages, so it relies on the security issues and mechanisms described for RPL. Still, it depends on information in several RPL protocol elements. If those were compromised, MRHOF might compute a wrong path and a packet could be misrouted. Deployments are therefore RECOMMENDED to use RPL security mechanisms when routing information might be modified or spoofed.

IANA allocated value 1 from the Objective Code Point (OCP) sub-registry of the RPL registry to MRHOF.
sections.eli5: If someone tells devices wrong distances, they pick a bad road, so important networks should lock down who can give directions.

viz.caption: RECOMMENDED PARAMETER VALUES WHEN ETX IS THE METRIC

cells: Disallow links with greater than 4 expected transmission counts
Disallow paths with greater than 256 expected transmission counts
Switch only if at least 1.5 fewer transmissions are expected
Two candidate parents remain if the preferred one is unavailable
Do not allow a node to become a floating root
